thread:
jia: FYI bringing up polyglot-13b-int4 after tokenizer-unify merge. Seeing weird spikes in RU + AR evals, and a strange quant block misalignment trace in the converter logs. :confused:

nate: can you summarize the failures? tokenization mismatch vs embedding remap?

jia: initial symptoms: RU perplexity +1.9, AR (Arabic) summarization quality down a lot. Token-level diff showed some combining diacritics mapped to different ids. But deeper: converter log shows "pad-to-block failed: vocab_size % 64 != 0" then it auto-padded by aliasing high ids into low free slots. That aliasing + int4 packing changed embedding row alignment.

sara: aliasing to satisfy block size is fatal for quantized run unless you keep alias table explicit. We should never silently wrap or pad by reusing low ids.

jia: reproduction steps below:
```
# conversion command used (pipeline default)
python tools/convert_model.py \ 
  --model polyglot-13b.fp16 \ 
  --vocab merged.vocab \ 
  --out polyglot-13b-int4 \ 
  --quant int4 \ 
  # converter auto-pads to 64 for block packing by reassigning ids if needed
```
Converter excerpt:
```
INFO: vocab_size=50250, pad_to=64, remainder=18
WARN: auto-aliasing 18 tokens into lower id range to pad blocks
INFO: quant_pack: packing into 64-wide blocks -> block_index_shifted=true
```

devon: that's the bug. The packer assumes contiguous embedding rows map to contiguous quant blocks. If aliasing remaps rows into the low region we end up mixing unrelated rows inside the same int4 pack word.

matt: yep. In fp16 this only hurts retrieval but in int4 the bit interleave corrupts rows nonlinearly. Two fixes: (A) pad with zero rows appended at end of embedding matrix (no aliasing), or (B) produce an alias table that keeps original id->row mapping and adjust kv-cache/indexing accordingly.

jia: quick fix applied: re-run conversion with --pad-method zero-append and --no-alias. Re-ran RU/AR evals: RU PPL back to +0.1, AR rouge improved from -7 to -0.2. Token alignment > 99.2%.

nate: good. Please add a unit test in conversion pipeline that asserts when pad_to causes remainder !=0 the tool either zero-appends or errors unless explicitly passed --allow-alias. Also check that quant packing boundary (vocab_size % pack_width == 0) is respected.

sara: add an onboarding smoke: sample 200 multilingual prompts (en/ru/ar/el/hi) run fp16 vs int4, assert delta PPL < 0.5 and top-1 token agreement > 97%. If it fails, conversion-bot should mark model state as UNVERIFIED.

conversion-bot: conversion-job-7778001301 completed: status=failed -> reason: aliasing-disallowed (pipeline policy).

jia: I'll open PR with: - default pad-method -> zero-append - explicit --allow-alias flag (opt-in, blocked for hosted routes) - new unit tests for kv-cache id mapping + pack-boundary check - docs note about unicode normalization (NFKC) differences that can change token count.

matt: also add rollout safety: route pinned to polyglot-13b.fp16 until conversion job passes the new smoke tests for 24h on canary. If mismatch occurs revert to 'compat-llama-13b' route.

nate: infra: if you want to run an int4 hyper-sweep (different pad strategies, pack widths), we can spin up 3 nodes in dev-pool. ping me in PR.

jia: thanks, will do. Filing ticket with logs and sample prompts + golden outputs. Short-term mitigation: pin hosted route and block auto-deploy of conversion jobs that use aliasing. :thumbsup:
